text:
This looks like mid-2008. Fed funds are near 2.0%, headline CPI is 4.1% (the July 2008 peak was 5.6%, so this is probably earlier), unemployment is 5.5%, and payrolls are negative.

Several details pin down the month:
- Unemployment was 5.5% in May 2008, and 5.0% in April.
- Headline CPI was 3.98% in April 2008 and 4.18% in May, so 4.08% is near either.
- The fed funds rate was about 2.0% in May and June 2008.
- The 2-year yield rose 1.03 points over three months, from about 1.6% in February to 2.65% in May.
- The 10-year yield was around 4.0% in May.
- US equities fell 8.4% in the month, which is too large for May 2008, when the S&P rose about 1%. June 2008 fell about 8.4%, which fits.
- In June 2008 the 2-year yield was about 2.9% and the 10-year about 4.0%, and the unemployment rate was 5.6%. Published unemployment was 5.5% in May, 5.6% in June.
- The 3-month change in fed funds of -0.52 fits June, since fed funds were 2.25% in March and 2.0% in June. Fed funds were also 2.0% in May.
- Headline CPI in June 2008 was 5.0%, which does not fit, so the CPI figure may be off. The 12m change in CPI of +1.4 means CPI a year earlier was 2.7%. June 2007 CPI was 2.7%, which fits June 2008. May 2007 CPI was 2.7% as well.
- The 12-month equity return of -13.2% fits June 2008, when the S&P was down about 13%.

The market data point to June 2008, so I take that, while accepting that the macro CPI and unemployment figures are slightly lagged or differ from published values.
